speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the prematurity at 33 weeks and the onset of respiratory distress shortly after birth, I suspect respiratory distress syndrome. What are the current oxygen saturation levels and blood gas results, and have you seen a chest X-ray yet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of grunting, retractions, and cyanosis in a 33-week preterm infant strongly suggests Respiratory Distress Syndrome due to surfactant deficiency. DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (NRDS)
